summary: 1933 CCC-built 14x14 L-4 groundhouse on Herd Peak, Klamath NF, Siskiyou County; staffed in the 1930s-1950s and today; NHLR-registered 1999; standing.

facts.design: classic 14 x 14 ft L-4 groundhouse with wooden catwalk; standard Forest Service 14 x 14 ft single-story house

staffing.status: staffed Sundays and Mondays May to October per NHLR; a 2019 visit found a sole resident lookout

access.note: Working Forest Service lookout. The register lists it as staffed on a schedule. No source says the public may enter the cab, so treat it as restricted until the Klamath National Forest says otherwise.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Goosenest Ranger District, Klamath National Forest

events.note: Register gives 1933. Clipping of 25 August 1933 says the lookout house was completed on 18 August by a CCC crew in twelve working days.
Earl J. Fain stationed at the lookout; the couple wintered in Dunsmuir after the season closed.
Bessie Cates spent four and a half months as the lookout.
Bessie Cates took the station for a third consecutive season.
Coast and Geodetic Survey station description of the lookout house, 14 x 14 ft standard Forest Service design, about 15 ft high.
Leona Andrus returned to Herd Peak Lookout on 27 October after a stint at Ball Mountain Lookout.
Date registered April 21, 1999 per the NHLR page.
An MK Library account of a 2019 visit describes Bob Clark as the tower's sole resident.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register lists Robert D. Clark staffing on Sundays and Mondays from May to October. An MK Library account of a 2019 visit describes Clark as the tower's sole resident. The sources do not say which pattern applies now, so the story reports both.
The register calls the site Herd Mountain Lookout, local clippings say Herd Peak, and a 1934 clipping says Hurd's peak. The story uses Herd Peak and notes the variants.

sources.title: Through the Eyes of a Fire Lookout

notes_for_editor: Brief's 1999 NHLR registration confirmed (April 21, 1999). Brief's 2105.6 m elevation matches the NHLR's 6,908 ft (2,106 m). A peakbagging.com search snippet gives 7,073 ft (2,156 m) for the same lookout; it was not read, so it is not used. Staffing: the NHLR schedule is undated; its only dated entry is an October 2, 2019 visit report by Robert D. Clark, and the MK Library account of a 2019 visit is the other dated observation, so the current staffing pattern is unconfirmed. Access level 'restricted' is a judgment from the working-station status; no source states visitor rules. No new photos found. Not verified: any Forest Service status page, any fire the lookout reported, any move or rebuild since 1958.
